application.name: ofetch-style HTTP client library
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client that wraps runtime fetch implementations to provide a higher-level $fetch/ofetch API with typed responses, option/header merging, automatic body serialization, response parsing, lifecycle hooks, retries, timeouts, and normalized FetchError objects. It provides browser/global and Node-specific entry points.
application.purpose: Developer infrastructure for making HTTP requests, not an end-user business application.

Variant that returns the full FetchResponse object, including parsed `_data`.
Passthrough to the underlying native fetch implementation.

A body value the client can automatically JSON.stringify and mark with JSON content-type/accept headers.

Normalizes a failed fetch context into a FetchError with a readable message and attached request/response/status/data metadata.
Determines whether an HTTP method can carry a request body, which affects JSON body handling and retry behavior.
Determines whether a request body should be treated as JSON-serializable so the client can stringify it and set JSON headers.
Chooses a response parser from the Content-Type header, defaulting to JSON when no content type is present.
Builds the effective request options by merging call options with defaults and resolving headers and query/params.

Core client factory. It creates the $fetch function and its raw/native/create variants, orchestrating option resolution, hooks, body handling, URL construction, timeout, response parsing, error handling, and retries.

Handles request failures: decides whether abort prevents retry, determines retry count/delay/status eligibility, retries through the raw fetch path, and throws a normalized FetchError when retries are exhausted or not applicable.
Creates the Node-specific fetch provider. It optionally enables keep-alive HTTP/HTTPS agents when FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE is set, otherwise uses the default node-fetch-native implementation.
Manual playground entry that calls $fetch against an external test endpoint and logs results/errors.
Test helper that aborts a request and verifies abort behavior during $fetch requests with retry configured.

applicationFacts: The library exports `ofetch` and `$fetch` from both global/browser and Node entry points.
`src/index.ts` selects globalThis/self/window/global fetch primitives and falls back to a rejecting function if global fetch is unavailable.
`src/node.ts` uses global fetch when available, otherwise node-fetch-native, and can create keep-alive agents for HTTP and HTTPS.
`createFetch` supports high-level `$fetch`, `$fetch.raw`, `$fetch.native`, and `$fetch.create` creation of derived clients with merged defaults.
JSON-serializable bodies for payload methods are automatically stringified and receive `content-type` and `accept: application/json` headers when absent.
Response parsing can be inferred from Content-Type, explicitly chosen via responseType, or overridden with parseResponse.
The error object exposes request, options, response, data, status, statusCode, statusText, and statusMessage metadata.
Retries are configurable by count, delay, and retryable status codes; payload methods default to zero retries while other methods default to one.
Timeouts are implemented by creating an AbortController signal and aborting with a TimeoutError cause.
Tests cover parsing, response types, binary handling, baseURL, JSON/non-JSON bodies, streams, FormData, URLSearchParams, 404/403/204/HEAD, retries, aborts, timeouts, default merging, and hooks.
Build configuration emits declarations and CJS output for `src/index` and `src/node`, treating `undici` as external.
